context:
Goal: you can always undo a recent check, and no control shows that does nothing.
Problem (rule): a (show on every ledger) shows a dead cell on an empty ledger; b (show only when the ledger holds data) hides the undo right after Reset empties the ledger, the moment it is needed. The record recent-checks-can-be-undone says b today.
Based on (ruling): 193 none (11:22 CST Nov 6): "neither of these seem correct from an outcome perspective". Asked again with an option keyed to the outcome.
Based on (ruling): recovery-control-not-state-gated: a recovery control must not depend on the state it recovers.
Based on (read): mailaudit src/app.jsx:6573-6576 says Reset shows on an empty ledger; recent-checks-can-be-undone.md:145 (main cd3e12f).
Departs from: the record (the cell shows only when the ledger holds data) — c shows it whenever something can be undone, Reset included.

lastAnswer.note: Routed 12:46 CST to the coordinator for a mailaudit lane: show the Recent cell while anything can be undone.

options.gain: The undo shows exactly when it works, also right after a Reset, and never as a dead cell.
options.label: Show while anything can be undone
options.lose: A mailaudit lane: the cell reads the undo list, not the ledger; if Reset itself cannot be undone yet, that lane adds it.

options.label: Show on every ledger
options.lose: The cell shows on an empty ledger, where it may do nothing.

options.label: Keep the data gate
options.lose: The undo hides after Reset empties the ledger, the day it is needed.

ref: deep audit 1102, mailaudit homes; coordinator handoff/audit-child-questions 9d97c9b, recent-cell-gate
title: mailaudit: when should the Recent cell (undo of recent checks) show?
why: Recommended: c. It ties the cell to what you can undo, the outcome, not to the ledger.
